pdf_evidence: The session graph is the partial order of (exercise, answer) pairs in one answering session. The heterogeneous relation graph links exercises, skills, and students. GGNN and GCN run on those graphs. The PDF does not define a free adjacency parameter.
changed_YN: The session graph is built from the observed answer order and then held fixed for message passing. It is not an expert map and it is not updated as a free adjacency during training. The eight-value record JOINTLY_LEARNED_TRAINING is not what this PDF states.

pdf_evidence: The basic graph is generated from the exercise sequence as a heterogeneous graph of question, knowledge, and learner nodes, with connections stored as E. A sampled heterogeneous graph is taken from that input sequence. TrueSkill scores are updated during training; the adjacency is not described as the updated object.

column12: Nodes and edges come from the exercise interaction record. No expert or curriculum map is supplied. The PDF does not make the adjacency a free parameter. The prior eight-value cell was empty, so this PDF reading is the record.

pdf_evidence: The SQC graph is defined over students, questions, and concepts. Student nodes are connected to the questions those students answered. Counterfactual replacement and disruption are later augmentations on that graph.
column11: The base graph is the observed student-question-concept relation. Counterfactual views are augmentations, not a free adjacency updated during training. The graph is not an expert map. The record JOINTLY_LEARNED_TRAINING overstates the PDF.

pdf_evidence: The logical-skill graph uses directed edges for the order of consecutive code submissions. The grammatical-skill graph encodes problems with CodeBERT, takes cosine similarity, and keeps pairs at or above a threshold t. Learnable symbols in Eqs. (5) and (7) are GNN weights, not the edge set. Manually annotated grammar appears only as a case-study comparison.
column10: Both graphs are constructed by the model from submission order and from CodeBERT cosine similarity. They are not a supplied expert, curriculum, or skill map. The edge set is fixed by that construction and by the threshold. It is not a free adjacency. The printed external-fixed label does not match this construction.

pdf_evidence: Two interaction graphs are built from historical interactions. The similarity adjacency is the sigmoid of the interaction-vector dot product, and an edge is kept only above the fixed threshold 0.5. The dissimilarity adjacency is J minus that matrix. The paper calls this the static view. Learnable W matrices are the graph-filter projections.
column10: The adjacency is a thresholded function of interaction vectors, not an expert map and not a free parameter matrix. The authors label the resulting state static. The record JOINTLY_LEARNED_TRAINING is not stated in the PDF.

pdf_evidence: Concept edges use the transition probability count(c_i to c_j) over count(c_i) in the learning sequence. Separate hypergraphs connect extrinsic-factor nodes and intrinsic-characteristic nodes when their cosine similarity exceeds a threshold. The addition-before-multiplication sentence is an example of why edges are directed.
column10: The concept graph is a transition count from learning sequences, and the hypergraphs are cosine-threshold graphs of recorded factors. Neither is a supplied expert map. Incidence matrices are inputs to later convolutions; they are not described as free parameters. The record EXTERNAL_FIXED is not what Eq. (5) computes.

pdf_evidence: Exercise-exercise edge weight is the co-correctness rate of students who attempted both exercises. Concept-concept edge weight is the co-mastery rate after an average-correctness comparison on the dataset. Graph optimal transport then aligns the source-domain and target-domain graphs.
column11: Edge weights are dataset rates, computed before alignment. Optimal transport minimizes a distance between the two graphs; the PDF does not update the adjacency as a free parameter. The graph is not an expert map. The printed dynamically-learned label does not match Eqs. (1)-(2).
